A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeDe and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably across layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original upstream detection and downstream classification experiments in Tables 1–5, alongside embedding visualizations, reconstructions, and error distributions.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds cross-paradigm embedding visualizations and a measured decoder-training runtime.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations 1–2 retain the same global/local embedding decoder, reconstruction loss, threshold, and inference masking rule. The CTRL noise-based treatment already appears in v1; v2 clarifies its description.

E1.justification: The CIFAR-10, ImageNet/CC3M, STL-10, GTSRB, and SVHN coverage and existing detection/classification tasks are retained. Figure 6 adds representation analysis for MAE and PixelCNN without reporting an additional dataset or DeDe detection task.

E2.justification: DECREE and ASSET remain the upstream baselines; downstream comparisons retain ASSET and the same clean/poisoned no-defense controls. The changed BadCLIP citation does not by itself establish a replacement experiment, and the added out-of-distribution references are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 revises the stated patch size from 4 at both image scales to a choice between 4 and 32. CTRL's reported ASR selection changes from the first epoch to the highest ASR. These are reported protocol revisions; unchanged table values do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds a t-SNE analysis of class clustering across CL, CLIP, MAE, and PixelCNN in Figure 6. Table 6's reconstruction examples and error histograms are unchanged; the new parameter-stability discussion does not introduce a separately displayed ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for the comparisons. The retained error histograms describe sample-level detection scores.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the reconstruction/error-distribution panels in Table 6 are unchanged. V2 adds Figure 6's clustering observations, a qualitative parameter-stability finding, and a DRUPE decoder-training runtime of 1 hour 11 minutes 30 seconds.

T1.justification: The formal encoder behavior, reconstruction objective, detection score, and algorithmic equations remain unchanged. The revised clustering rationale is conceptual explanation, with no added theorem, proof, or formal derivation.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly adds encoder non-invasiveness as a claimed advantage in the introduction and conclusion. The central claims about decoder-based detection, flexible auxiliary data, and effectiveness against CL/CLIP backdoors remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 extends the interpretation of downstream-training dependence from CTRL to BadCLIP. Its appendix newly recommends masking ratios of 0.75–0.95 based on claimed stability and uses cross-paradigm clustering to support DeDe's rationale.

D1.justification: Section 5 adds a public DeDe code-repository statement. V2 also documents resizing and color augmentation, and Appendix B discloses frozen-encoder training, a 50k-image dataset, a 200-epoch budget, Xeon/RTX 4090 hardware, and runtime. These add reproducibility information without establishing changes to the underlying runs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Generalized ODIN, OpenOOD, and an out-of-distribution detection survey, briefly connecting their pipelines to backdoor-sample detection. It also changes the experimental BadCLIP attribution from Bai et al.'s prompt-learning paper to Liang et al.'s dual-embedding paper; both works were already cited in v1.

P1.justification: V2 revises the abstract and Section 4.2 explanation, makes scattered language corrections, organizes the appendix into sections A and B, and updates affiliations and acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figure 6, adjusts labeling and presentation in Figures 2 and 5, clarifies table captions and row labels, and adds result highlighting. Appendix Tables 3–6 are regrouped onto one page while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: The added code-access statement, concrete training and preprocessing details, and clearer explanations and displays improve transparency and usability. The gains are limited: central performance evidence is unchanged, and the new parameter-stability assertion lacks a separately reported quantitative sweep.
